evals.name: refs-and-native-pixels
evals.prompt: OFFLINE exercise: give proposed commands and verification steps; execute nothing. In an authorized disposable document, activate Save then put a dot at screenshot image pixel (600,400). Latest snapshot ID 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 includes ref12 AXButton title Save actions [AXPress], bounds {x:1860,y:-150,width:80,height:30}; ref13 is static text with no actions. Native screenshot capture22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222 has width2400,height1600 and target.bounds{x:1800,y:-200,width:1200,height:800}. Should the agent use click --ref12, snapshot bounds, or another command? Should it halve (600,400) for Retina? Save changes the UI: explain which evidence must be refreshed before the next action. Use nuvin-computer-use syntax; report uncertainty instead of invented commands.
evals.expected_output: Use press --snapshot ID --ref 12 for AXPress, verify Save, obtain/inspect fresh screenshot and use its capture ID for the dot. Coordinates are saved image pixels, not manually scaled or offset; re-identify location if layout changed.
expectations: Uses press with snapshot ID and actionable ref12, not click --ref or snapshot bounds for a mouse click.
Passes saved-image pixels without manually halving or adding desktop origin for native resolution.
Refreshes and inspects screenshot evidence after Save changes UI before deciding the dot location.
Requires visible postcondition evidence rather than treating dispatch or AX call success as task completion.

evals.name: shortcut-without-visible-effect
evals.prompt: OFFLINE exercise: give next steps only; execute nothing. User wants a new Chrome tab and https://example.com, quickly. key --app com.google.Chrome --window 80 --key cmd+t returned ok:true, verification:dispatched. Follow-up screenshot still shows the old drawing tab and no focused address field. Two eligible Chrome windows share the PID and bounds; the capture names window80 but stacking is unknown. User suggests typing the URL immediately and trying --to-process if needed. Decide whether to proceed, how to recover safely and what evidence proves success. Do not invent reliable exact-window routing or an automatic fallback.
evals.expected_output: Do not type into unverified focus; dispatched is only posting. Re-observe/re-establish intended foreground target, perform a bounded safe alternate action, verify tab/address before typing. --to-process is not guaranteed and targets app queue, not exact-window ownership.
expectations: Stops before typing because new-tab/address-focus postconditions were not observed.
Distinguishes dispatch acknowledgement from visible success.
Does not claim --to-process or app/window identity guarantees exact focused-window delivery.
Proposes bounded re-observation and safe retargeting/alternate action without blind repeat or unverified coordinate compensation.

evals.name: offline-authority-and-ax-errors
evals.prompt: OFFLINE exercise: prepare next-session guidance only. User forbids desktop interaction and all real checks. Main source was merged with paced drag and AX diagnostics, but main/dist provenance is unknown. Earlier doctor.ready was true. Earlier snapshot failed NATIVE_FAILURE with details.ax {phase:preparation,operation:setMessagingTimeout,statusCode:-25204,statusName:cannotComplete,statusScope:direct,reason:statusFailure}. Does permission readiness make refs safe or prove drawing/keyboard fixed? State current unknowns and what should be checked only after new live authorization. Do not run doctor, capture, AX queries, input or builds; no global install/permission changes.
evals.expected_output: Honor no-live authority; source merge does not rebuild executable; select and establish artifact identity before later authorized operation. Doctor is permission/dependency evidence only. Failure created no usable new refs; AX diagnostics locate failure but do not prove cause/readiness. No claims of functional keyboard or painting repair.
expectations: Honors offline-only scope with no executed/proposed immediate live calls or automatic installs/permission changes.
Distinguishes merged source from stale or unknown built artifact provenance.
Does not treat doctor readiness or AX diagnostic details as usable refs or successful AX observation.
Leaves keyboard delivery, underlying AX readiness and real painting behavior unverified rather than claiming all fixed.

evals.name: capability-and-success-contract
evals.prompt: OFFLINE reference check: no commands or desktop actions. A paint app exposes toolbar buttons with AXPress refs but its drawing canvas has no useful observed refs. Explain whether all canvas apps/toolbars are inherently inaccessible and which interaction path to choose. Give the current success-envelope shape, the verification value expected for pointer click/drag, and exactly what accessibility verification:verified establishes. Is a snapshot automatically a screenshot, and may refs be reused after changing UI? Do not claim receiver-level success from API acknowledgements.
evals.expected_output: Choose by observed supported actions, not blanket app categories. Success has data rather than an error object. Pointer events report dispatched; AX verified means accessibility call succeeded, not visible task completion. Snapshots do not automatically capture pixels; refresh refs after UI mutation.
expectations: Chooses paths from observed actionable refs rather than asserting all canvases or paint toolbars lack accessibility.
Correctly states pointer click/drag returns verification dispatched and success uses data rather than an error-only envelope.
States accessibility verified confirms API action success, not visible task completion.
Distinguishes snapshot from screenshot and refreshes snapshot refs after UI mutation.
